facts.text: A family member checks the weather on a smartphone before leaving for work.
People use video calls to see relatives who live far away.
A teenager plugs in a phone at night because its battery runs low by evening.
Many households connect phones, televisions, and computers to the same wireless router.
A smart television opens streaming services without a separate disc player.
People search through several streaming services to find a program they want to watch.
Wireless earbuds need charging and can be misplaced easily.
A smartwatch can show incoming messages and track daily steps.
A driver plugs a smartphone into the car to display maps and directions.
A delivery driver checks a phone for the next address on the route.
A cashier turns a card reader toward the customer for a tap payment.
Some shoppers pay at a register by holding a phone near the payment terminal.
A restaurant customer scans a square code to read the menu on a phone.
Many shops offer online ordering with pickup at the counter or curb.
A customer receives a text message when an online order is ready for collection.
A home security camera sends a phone alert when someone approaches the front door.
A voice-controlled speaker can set a kitchen timer or answer a simple question.
A student submits homework through a school website instead of handing in every assignment on paper.
A household printer may sit unused for weeks until someone needs a paper form.
An office worker joins a video meeting from a laptop at the kitchen table.
Some office workers share files through online storage rather than carrying a flash drive.
A weak wireless signal can interrupt a video meeting or a streamed program.
A phone user receives repeated reminders to install software updates.
A person must remember passwords or use a password manager for numerous online accounts.
A family may have a robot vacuum that moves around furniture and returns to its charging dock.
A teenager uses a phone camera to record and edit a short video.
People use online appointment systems for medical visits and other local services.
Some residents ask a conversational artificial intelligence program to draft text or explain a question.
